question.text: Herd mentality in markets refers to:

answer.text: Carefully researched investment decisions made independently
Investors following the crowd without independent analysis, amplifying market bubbles and crashes

explanation.text: The Logic: Herd mentality is the tendency of investors to follow the choices of others rather than independent analysis. Pages 198, 242, and 244 of the NISM Series XV Research Analyst workbook (February 2026) explain that this behaviour can drive prices away from fundamentals and lead to market bubbles and subsequent crashes. The Trap: Carefully researched independent decisions, deliberate diversification, and contrarian strategies are the opposite of herd behaviour, not examples of it. Note: Specific FOMO-buying and panic-selling labels, and the often-quoted Buffett "fearful when others are greedy" line, were not found in the pages checked and are therefore not used here.
